findings.title: Admin login — dashboard loads, sidebar visible
findings.evidence: app/api/admin/login/route.ts:44-153: service-role lookup of admin_users by email (bypasses RLS), rejects suspended (60-62) and must_set_password/no-hash (63-74), verifies legacy SHA-256 hash (78-81), lazy-provisions+links auth.users (83-119), signs in via anon client to mint a session (121-137), returns {session,admin} (139-153). components/AuthGate.tsx:187-294 login() POSTs to that route then supabase.auth.setSession (250-253) and sets authed=true, rendering the app shell/sidebar. Functionally correct. Caveat: the primary credential check is an UNSALTED SHA-256 (login/route.ts:78-81); auth.users bcrypt is only secondary — a security weakness, not a functional failure.
findings.prodNote: Log in with your own admin credentials (or a disposable admin). First-ever login lazy-writes admin_users.user_id (idempotent). No charges/emails/3rd-party side effects.

findings.title: Wrong password 5x → 30-min lockout + unlock email
findings.concern: The 30-min lockout and unlock email are implemented ONLY client-side in localStorage — trivially bypassable (localStorage.clear(), a different browser, or curl straight at /api/admin/login). There is no per-account server-side lockout: grep found NO locked_until/failed_attempts columns on admin_users (those columns exist only on otp_attempts, for OTP). Server-side the only protection is a per-IP rate limit (429 after 5/15min) which is IP-based and sends no email. Known/tracked gap.
findings.evidence: components/AuthGate.tsx:11-12 (MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, LOCKOUT_DURATION=30min), :227-233 increments localStorage ck_fail_count and at >=5 sets ck_lock_until + calls sendResetEmail (:296-310 -> sendAdminSetupLink RESET). No server-side lockout in app/api/admin/login/route.ts. Only proxy.ts:148 AUTH_LIMIT (5 / 15min per IP -> 429). Documented as a defect in docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS_PHASE_2.md (J4-M2) and PHASE_5 (P2-7). In a single browser the expected UX (locked screen + reset email) does occur.
findings.prodNote: Triggering the 5th failure calls sendResetEmail, which sends a REAL setup/reset email to the target admin address, and consumes the per-IP auth rate-limit budget (could 429 real logins from that IP). Use a disposable admin email you control, or assert the lockout UI via the e2e simulateLockout helper and DB-confirm that admin_users has no lockout columns.

verification.note: Every auditor citation verified in code. components/AuthGate.tsx:11 MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, :12 LOCKOUT_DURATION=30*60*1000 (30min). Lockout is purely client-side localStorage: :227-228 increments ck_fail_count, :230-233 at failCount>=5 sets ck_lock_until (localStorage) + setLocked(true) + sendResetEmail(); :296-307 sendResetEmail looks up admin_users and calls sendAdminSetupLink(admin,"RESET","") (a password reset/setup link, not a literal "unlock" email). checkLockout() (:50-58) reads ck_lock_until from localStorage — trivially defeated by localStorage.clear()/new browser. Server-side app/api/admin/login/route.ts has NO per-account lockout: on hash mismatch (:79-81) it returns 401 "Invalid credentials" with zero attempt counting; the selected admin_users columns (:47-49) contain no lockout fields, and no code writes any. Confirmed the ONLY server-side protection is a per-IP rate limit: proxy.ts:148 AUTH_LIMIT {limit:5, windowMs:15*60_000}, applied to /api/admin/login at :226-228 keyed by getClientIp (:132-138), returning 429 at :239-256 with NO email sent (and E2E_BYPASS_RATE_LIMIT=1 short-circuits it at :222; in-memory fallback at :232/235 is per-instance/best-effort). Grep confirms locked_until exists ONLY on otp_attempts (supabase/migrations/20260509120000_otp_attempt_tracking.sql:13,40,49-55), NOT admin_users. Gap is explicitly tracked: docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS_PHASE_2.md:187 (J4-M2) and :234 + PHASE_5.md:80 (P2-7), both prescribing a server-side admin_users.locked_until fix. So the single-browser UX (locked screen + reset email) genuinely fires, but the security control is client-only and bypassable — PARTIAL is accurate; not WIRED (no server enforcement) and not MISSING (client UX + email do exist).

findings.title: Suspended subscription → access blocked, 'subscription suspended' shown
findings.concern: The suspension gate is entirely client-side UI. There is no server-side data gate: app/lib/api-auth.ts:39-52 requireActiveSubscription is DEFINED BUT NEVER CALLED (grep: only the definition) and it reads a different table (subscriptions.status) than what the UI uses (businesses.subscription_status). proxy.ts does not check subscription. So while the dashboard UI blocks and shows the suspended screen, direct API/supabase calls still return data when a tenant is SUSPENDED (RLS does not consider subscription status).
findings.evidence: Migration supabase/migrations/20260319130600_subscription_status.sql:3-4 adds businesses.subscription_status (default ACTIVE; comment 'checked by AuthGate'). components/AuthGate.tsx:421-446: if subscriptionStatus SUSPENDED|PAUSED && role!==SUPER_ADMIN && not (/billing & MAIN_ADMIN) -> renders 'Your account has been suspended' and blocks children; status read in loadBusinessContext (:67,:87,:99). AppShell.tsx:59-60 also route-blocks when suspended. Expected UX is met client-side only.
findings.prodNote: Flipping businesses.subscription_status=SUSPENDED on a live business locks a real operator out of their dashboard. Use a disposable/staging tenant (or flip on a test business and revert immediately); verify the AuthGate suspended screen AND separately confirm (DB/API) that data still returns while suspended to document the missing server-side gate.

findings.title: Generate slots (date range, tour, time, days, capacity) → slots appear on calendar
findings.evidence: Two entry points. '+ Add Slot' (app/slots/page.tsx:731-734 → saveAddSlot:604-667) upserts slots with business_id/status OPEN, onConflict business_id,tour_id,start_time, and converts time correctly via zonedToUtc(getAdminTimezone()) (:614,:624) — BUT it has no day-of-week selector, creating a slot for every day in the range (:620). 'Bulk Generate' (app/slots/page.tsx:737-740 → components/BulkSlotWizard.tsx → app/lib/slot-generation.ts) DOES have day-of-week (matches the checklist's 'days') but is timezone-buggy: slot-generation.ts:27 derives the date via d.toISOString() (shifts by a day when the browser is not UTC) and :32 hardcodes localDate.setHours(getHours()-2) on a locally-parsed Date. For a SAST (UTC+2) admin browser this stores slots ~2h earlier (and can roll the date back a day). Slots appear on the calendar but at the wrong time/date via the bulk path.
findings.prodNote: Pure DB upserts, reversible (delete slots). Safe to run; verify resulting start_time values in DB.
findings.concern: BulkSlotWizard (the 'days' path) uses hardcoded -2h offset + toISOString() date extraction instead of the tenant timezone helpers used by saveAddSlot — wrong slot times/dates for non-UTC (real SAST) operators.

findings.title: Bulk edit slots across a date range → all matching slots updated
findings.evidence: app/slots/page.tsx:534-602 saveBulkEdit builds baseUpdates {capacity_total, price_per_person_override} and applies them over a date range: plain path :579-583 does .update(baseUpdates).gte(startDate).lte(endDate) with .eq("tour_id",...) ONLY when tourId!=='ALL' (:585). When tourId==='ALL' the UPDATE has neither a tour filter NOR an explicit .eq("business_id", ...) — it relies solely on the slots RLS UPDATE policy to prevent cross-tenant writes (the exact pattern CLAUDE.md flags). Functionally all matching slots are updated and load() refreshes (:596).

findings.concern: Bulk UPDATE on business-scoped slots omits explicit business_id filter (tourId='ALL' path has no tenant/tour predicate at all); safe only because RLS is enforced. Also uses .lte('...T23:59:59') naive timestamp bounds (no tz), which can miss/include edge slots near midnight.

Greyed/hidden in admin: WeekView shows closed slots red with a 'Closed' badge (components/WeekView.tsx:126-135) and the list hides them by default (app/slots/page.tsx:673).

Test by closing an EMPTY slot (no bookings → no messages), or seed a disposable booking with your own phone/email on a staging tenant.

findings.concern: Cross-tenant isolation gap: voucher lookup (309) filters .eq('code', code) only, and RLS vouchers_anon_select (migration 20260509100000:42-48) matches ONLY x-voucher-code header — no business_id predicate. confirm_voucher_booking RPC (20260530120000:79-118) redeems p_voucher_ids without verifying vouchers.business_id = bookings.business_id. verification.note: Auditor's PARTIAL is accurate on both axes. FUNCTIONAL (works, single-tenant): booking/app/book/page.tsx computes effectiveVoucherCredit and finalTotal=max(0,afterPromoTotal-effectiveVoucherCredit) at 268-277; per-voucher applied/remaining rendered 883-903 — credit correctly deducted. findings.title: Reschedule hold expiry — new slot hold released, original booking unchanged
findings.evidence: supabase/functions/cron-tasks/index.ts:16-107 cleanupExpiredHolds: selects ACTIVE holds with expires_at < now-5min grace (22-30); for hold_type==='RESCHEDULE' that is not paid it sets hold EXPIRED (59), finds the linked pending_reschedules PENDING (63-67), marks them EXPIRED (70-73), releases the new slot's held capacity via adjust_slot_capacity RPC held_delta=-qty with a business_id+id-scoped direct-update fallback (78-92), logs reschedule_upgrade_expired (94-99), and explicitly sends NO WhatsApp (105). Paid-in-grace guard (38-52) converts the hold instead of expiring if the pending_reschedule already COMPLETED or the booking is PAID.
findings.concern: Effective release is ~20 min (15-min hold + 5-min grace) plus the next 5-min cron tick, not exactly 15 min as the case wording implies — at 15 min the hold is still ACTIVE. This is the intended grace window (CLAUDE.md), but a tester waiting exactly 15 min would see nothing yet. Also depends on cron-tasks actually being scheduled.

findings.title: Schedule campaign: fires at set time
findings.evidence: For a scheduled send, sendCampaign inserts the marketing_queue rows IMMEDIATELY with status 'pending' regardless of isScheduled (app/marketing/templates/page.tsx:271-278; the insert is unconditional). The per-minute cron marketing-dispatch (migration 20260323200100_marketing_dispatch_cron.sql) calls claim_marketing_queue which selects rows WHERE status='pending' and flips them to 'processing' with no campaign-status filter (supabase/migrations/20260511044907_scale_readiness_hardening.sql:124-142). marketing-dispatch then SKIPS items whose campaign is not yet 'sending' via `continue` (supabase/functions/marketing-dispatch/index.ts:121-124), leaving them stuck in 'processing'. There is NO code anywhere that resets stale 'processing' rows back to 'pending' (verified: grep for 'processing'/processing_started_at across supabase/ finds only the claim RPC and the fallback set). When scheduled_at finally passes, step 0 flips the campaign to 'sending' (:55-58) but claim only picks 'pending' rows — all rows are now 'processing' — so 0 emails are ever sent. Bug triggers for any campaign scheduled more than ~1 minute out (i.e. every real schedule).
findings.concern: Queue rows for future-scheduled campaigns are consumed into 'processing' on the next cron tick and never sent; the campaign shows 'Scheduled' then silently delivers nothing. Fix: only enqueue at fire time, or have claim/skip re-set skipped rows to 'pending'.

RPC (20260308120000_external_booking.sql:313-354) inserts bookings row with source=upper(p_source), external_ref, status default PAID; capacity taken atomically via conditional UPDATE ...WHERE status='OPEN' AND (capacity_total-booked-held)>=p_qty (L278-284). business_id derived from HMAC/api-key auth, not client-supplied.
findings.concern: The stored source column is whatever x-source / body.source the partner sends (uppercased, normalizeSource index.ts:104-108) — it is only literally 'EXTERNAL' if the caller/credential uses that source string (admin UI defaults source to 'VIATOR', ExternalBookingSettings.tsx:72). Not a bug, but 'source EXTERNAL' is caller-dependent, not hardcoded.
findings.prodNote: PAID bookings trigger a real WhatsApp (send-whatsapp-text) + email (send-email) when phone/email present (index.ts:827-883); PENDING/HELD triggers a real Yoco create-checkout (index.ts:801). Test on a throwaway tenant with Yoco test mode, omit phone/email or use your own disposable contacts, then assert bookings.source/external_ref via DB.

findings.title: Modify external booking updates slot/qty atomically
findings.evidence: index.ts:927-987: requires external_ref, validates new_date/new_time, looks up existing via getBookingByExternalRef (index.ts:415-424, tenant-scoped business_id+source+external_ref), resolves target tour/slot tenant-scoped, calls ck_external_modify_booking (index.ts:950). RPC (20260308120000_external_booking.sql:451-610) locks booking FOR UPDATE, applies qty delta with capacity guard on same slot, or slot-move (increment new with capacity guard + release old), updates booking fields; returns updated row. Rejects modifying CANCELLED (BOOKING_CANCELLED) and closed/full target slots.
findings.prodNote: No notifications are sent by the modify path, but it irreversibly mutates a live booking and slot capacity. Seed a disposable booking on a throwaway tenant, modify it, and assert via DB.

findings.title: Cancel external booking releases capacity, idempotent
findings.evidence: index.ts:902-925: requires external_ref, calls ck_external_cancel_booking (index.ts:906). RPC (20260308120000_external_booking.sql:393-449) selects booking FOR UPDATE by business_id+source+external_ref; not found -> BOOKING_NOT_FOUND (404 index.ts:916); already CANCELLED -> idempotent BOOKING_ALREADY_CANCELLED; releases held or booked capacity on the slot; sets status=CANCELLED, cancelled_at, cancellation_reason. Tenant-scoped throughout.
findings.prodNote: No messages sent, but irreversibly cancels a live booking and mutates slot capacity. Seed a disposable booking on a throwaway tenant and cancel it; DB-assert status=CANCELLED and slot capacity restored.

findings.title: Duplicate external_ref is idempotent (returns existing)
findings.evidence: ck_external_create_booking pre-checks an existing row by (business_id, source, external_ref) and returns code ALREADY_EXISTS with the existing booking_id/status BEFORE any insert (20260308120000_external_booking.sql:259-276). Backed by unique index bookings_external_ref_unique_idx on (business_id,source,external_ref) WHERE external_ref IS NOT NULL (migration L21-23). Concurrent-insert race is caught by the unique_violation handler which rolls back the slot booked increment and returns the existing booking (migration L364-390). Edge fn returns idempotent:true and skips confirmation WA/email/checkout for ALREADY_EXISTS via the code!=='ALREADY_EXISTS' guard (index.ts:797, 886-898).
findings.prodNote: Re-POSTing an EXISTING external_ref returns ALREADY_EXISTS with no new charge/message/mutation. Reuse the external_ref of a booking you already seeded (do NOT invent a fresh ref, which would create a real booking); assert idempotent:true and identical booking_id.

findings.title: Invalid API key / wrong HMAC signature -> 401
findings.evidence: verifyAuth (index.ts:256-291) is called at index.ts:637 BEFORE any action handler (HMAC-before-logic holds). Returns 401 for: missing key (MISSING_API_KEY), no matching active credential (INVALID_API_KEY, findCredentialByApiKey index.ts:218-254 matches sha256(api_key)), missing x-timestamp/x-signature (MISSING_SIGNATURE), non-numeric ts (INVALID_TIMESTAMP), >300s skew (STALE_SIGNATURE index.ts:280), and wrong signature (INVALID_SIGNATURE) using constant-time safeEqual (index.ts:194-199); all emitted via send(401,...) at index.ts:641-643. Signature = HMAC_SHA256(secret, `${ts}.${rawBody}`) over raw bytes (index.ts:285). verify_jwt=false (config.toml:10-11) so the gateway does not pre-reject partner calls.
findings.concern: (A) Config-dependent: HMAC is only enforced when the credential row has an hmac_secret; an api-key-only credential silently accepts ANY or missing signature (index.ts:263-266). Default seeding and the admin UI default HMAC on (ExternalBookingSettings.tsx:83), so the default is enforced. (B) Deploy landmine affecting ALL of Y1-Y6: migration 20260502120000_...phase2.sql:20-21 DROPS the plaintext external_booking_credentials.hmac_secret column, but findCredentialByApiKey still SELECTs that column (index.ts:222) and ExternalBookingSettings.tsx:147 selects it too — if phase2 is applied, every request throws and returns 500 (not 401) and the admin page breaks. Evidence it is not yet applied: index.ts was edited in acf5d4a AFTER phase2 was committed in 42067a1 while still selecting the plaintext column, so the live column is presumably still present; a future `supabase db push` would apply phase2 and break auth. (C) Minor: on valid-key+bad-signature, beginEventLog writes an audit row before the 401 (index.ts:637-640) — not strictly 'zero DB writes', though it is an idempotent audit log, not business logic; the invalid-key path writes nothing.
findings.prodNote: Produces only 401 responses (plus, for valid-key+bad-sig, one idempotent audit-log row) — no charge/message/booking mutation. Bogus x-api-key needs no setup; to test the wrong-signature 401 you need a valid API key for a disposable tenant whose credential has an hmac_secret.

findings.title: RLS data isolation (Tenant A cannot see Tenant B data)
findings.evidence: Verified against LIVE prod (project ukdsrndqhsatjkmxijuj) via read-only pg_policies/pg_proc queries. current_business_ids() (live def): SECURITY DEFINER, resolves admin via admin_users.user_id=auth.uid(); returns array_agg(all businesses.id) for role LIKE 'SUPER%', else the admin's own business_id(s), else '{}' (default-deny). Core tables are correctly tenant-scoped for authenticated: bookings/invoices/customers/conversations/chat_messages/refund_requests/admin_users/vouchers all have policies USING (business_id = ANY(current_business_ids())). A global check for policyname ILIKE 'Allow all operations%' returned ZERO rows — the permissive USING(true) FOR ALL policy from 20260304150000_enable_rls_all.sql has been removed on live. Anon paths are narrowed (bookings_anon_select is token/method-gated; vouchers_anon_select requires x-voucher-code header). GAP 1: reviews (business_id uuid NOT NULL, a business-scoped table) has reviews_authenticated_read SELECT USING(true) AND reviews_authenticated_update UPDATE USING(true) -> any authenticated admin can read AND modify EVERY tenant's reviews. GAP 2: vouchers_anon_update has qual=true / with_check=true and anon holds GRANT UPDATE (supabase/migrations/20260506051500_fix_bookings_anon_select_update_policies.sql:18-19), so the public anon key can update any voucher across tenants. combo_bookings/combo_offers public SELECT true and plans public read true are acceptable (combo is the sanctioned cross-tenant flow; plans is a global catalog).
findings.concern: reviews leaks cross-tenant (read+write) to any authenticated user, directly violating 'no cross-tenant data visible'; vouchers allows anon cross-tenant writes. Also reproducibility risk: current_business_ids() and the permissive-policy drops for bookings/invoices/customers/holds/conversations/etc. are NOT in any checked-in migration (only slots/tours/vouchers/businesses drops exist, in 20260509100000). The live DB was hardened out-of-band and is ahead of the repo, so a fresh `supabase db reset`/migrate would fail (policies reference an undefined function) or reproduce the old insecure state. docs/ISOLATION_TEST_REPORT.md PASS is dated 2026-04-17 and predates the May RLS policy set, so it does not validate the current policies.
findings.prodNote: Read-only: inspect pg_policies/pg_proc, or role-switch (SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated + request.jwt.claims.sub=<other-tenant admin user_id>) and SELECT — never write. To confirm the reviews leak: as a Tenant A admin session, SELECT * FROM reviews and check rows from other business_ids appear.
findings.existingTest: none (no automated RLS/cross-tenant test in tests/e2e or tests/unit; only the manual, now-stale docs/ISOLATION_TEST_REPORT.md)

So the single-browser UX (locked screen + reset email) genuinely fires, but the security control is client-only and bypassable — PARTIAL is accurate; not WIRED (no server enforcement) and not MISSING (client UX + email do exist).
